hypothesis: Among the six distinct valid programs in the catalog, 32x16 measured 2.901 μs, 16x32 measured 3.128 μs, and the selected 16x64 parent measured 3.249 μs; those results do not establish a cause. This experiment holds the 32-wide x pencil fixed and expands the y output tile from 16 to 32 rows. It halves the y-tile count and relative radius-4 halo duplication (50% to 25% of core rows), but doubles threads per block from 512 to 1024 and increases shared memory per block. The competing effects on block count, halo traffic, and occupancy require measurement; no winner is presumed.
notes: One bounded geometry experiment: 32x32 output tiles with radius-4 shared-memory halos loaded from the existing input buffer. The period-63 y endpoint mapping and stencil arithmetic are preserved. The controller should validate signed inputs and measure full-run event latency; no candidate performance result is claimed here.
transformations: Set the x pencil width and y output tile height to 32, launching a 32x32 block over x pencils, y subtiles, and z planes.
Load radius-4 lower and upper halo rows directly from the existing input, wrapping out-of-domain halo rows with the baseline period-(my-1) endpoint convention.
Use one barrier after center and halo loads; preserve the stencil coefficients, arithmetic expression, output coverage, buffers, entry point, and launch model.
